Cross-references World History (the imperial bridge) and hands off to Art History (the object register), Archaeology (the material record) and Political Science (the Constitution’s history).

chapters.title: The Sources and the Periodisation
chapters.summary: India’s history’s evidence: the archaeological register (sites, inscriptions, coins, monuments), the literary register (the Vedas to the medieval chronicles, their dating problems), the foreign accounts (Megasthenes, Fa-Hien, Hiuen Tsang, Al-Biruni and the Europeans); the periodisation debate — the ancient/medieval/modern triad as a colonial-era convention interrogated honestly against the indigenist alternatives; and the map of this book’s twelve-chapter arc.

chapters.title: Prehistoric and Harappan India
chapters.summary: The Palaeolithic stations of the subcontinent (the Sohan and Madras industries), the Mesolithic microliths and the Neolithic-chalcolithic villages of the Deccan and the Ganga valley; the Harappan civilisation in full — town planning (the grid, the great bath, the drainage), society and economy (the seals, the weights, the trade with Mesopotamia), the major sites’ census, the script’s undeciphered honesty, and the decline’s competing theories (climate, the river’s shift, the ’Aryan’ question retired carefully).
plannedLessons: The Harappan Town and Its Craft

chapters.title: The Vedic World and the Second Urbanisation
chapters.summary: The Vedic corpus as social evidence — the Rigveda’s pastoral world, the later Vedic’s agrarian turn, the varna system’s elaboration, the Upanishadic turn of thought; the sixth-century BCE’s second urbanisation (the Ganga cities, iron, coinage) and its two great dissents — Mahavira’s Jainism and the Buddha’s path with their sanghas and the Pali canon; and the sixteen Mahajanapadas’ politics ending at the Nandas.

chapters.title: From the Mauryas to the Guptas
chapters.summary: The Mauryan empire: Chandragupta and Kautilya’s Arthashastra, Ashoka’s inscriptions and dhamma, the administration-economy-art census and Megasthenes’ account; the post-Mauryan arrivals — the Indo-Greeks, the Shakas, the Kushanas and the Satavahanas with the three art schools (Gandhara, Mathura, Amaravati); the imperial Guptas’ golden-age question priced honestly (administration, the sciences, the arts); and Harsha’s Kanauj as the ancient arc’s close.
plannedLessons: The Mauryan State and Ashoka’s Dhamma
The Post-Mauryan World and the Art Schools
The Guptas and the Golden-Age Question

chapters.title: The Early Medieval South
chapters.summary: The peninsular powers the northern chronicles skip: the Age of the Three Empires (800-1000) — the Rashtrakutas, the Pratiharas and the Palas in their tripartite struggle; the Cholas’ state (the village assemblies’ uttaramerur evidence, the navy, the Rajendra raids), the temple as the era’s economic and cultural engine; the southeast-Asian cultural reach (the Pallava-Chola hands in the Khmer and Srivijaya worlds); and the regional kingdoms’ census across the peninsula.
plannedLessons: The Chola State and Its Assemblies

chapters.title: The Delhi Sultanate
chapters.summary: The five dynasties — the Mamluks, the Khaljis, the Tughlaqs, the Sayyids and the Lodis — with their character (the market reforms and the capital experiments priced as both bold and failed); the Sultanate’s administration (iqta, the ministries), its economy and its society; the Mongol containment; the Sultanate’s architecture (the arch and the dome arrive — the Qutb, the Lodi tombs); and the peninsular answer — Vijayanagar and the Bahmanis’ long duel.

chapters.title: The Mughal Empire
chapters.summary: Babur to Aurangzeb as one arc: the establishment (Panipat, the Humayun interregnum, Sher Shah’s administration), Akbar’s synthesis (the sulah-i-kul, the mansabdari engine, the Rajput alliance), Jahangir and Shah Jahan’s culture, Aurangzeb’s expansion and its costs; the empire’s institutions priced (the jagir crisis honestly); the art-and-architecture register (the Fatehpur Sikri, the Taj, the atelier) with the depth handed to Art History; the Rajputs and the Marathas’ rise (Shivaji’s swarajya); and the decline’s historiography.
plannedLessons: The Marathas and the Decline’s Historiography

chapters.title: The Eighteenth Century
chapters.summary: The post-Mughal regional order — the successor states (Bengal, Awadh, Hyderabad, the Sikhs, the Jats, the Rohillas) and the eighteenth-century debate (was it a ’dark age’? no — priced against the scholarship); the European companies’ arrival as traders; the Carnatic wars; Plassey and Buxar as the conquest’s hinge; the British consolidation’s policies and their economic, administrative and socio-cultural impact (the drain priced honestly) — the bridge where this book and World History’s imperial arc meet.
plannedLessons: The Carnatic Wars and the Companies

chapters.title: Colonial Rule and the Response
chapters.summary: The colonial state’s construction: the acts from 1773 to 1858 and the Crown’s Raj (the Political Science book owns the constitutional history’s analytical register); the socio-religious reform movements (Raja Rammohan Roy, the Brahmo Samaj, the Arya Samaj, the Aligarh movement, the Singh Sabha — the reform-and-revival distinction); the deindustrialisation and the railways’ double face; and the 1857 revolt in full — causes, leaders, nature, suppression, consequences (the GS1 line carried verbatim in spirit).
plannedLessons: The Acts and the Raj’s Construction
The Reform and the Revival Movements
The Rise of Indian Nationalism and the Moderates
The Gandhian Phase and Mass Movements
The Constitution, Partition and Integration of States

chapters.title: The Freedom Struggle
chapters.summary: The national movement’s whole arc as the GS1 register demands: the growth of nationalism (the unification’s engines — railways, press, education), the Moderates’ era, the Swadeshi and the Surat split, the revolutionary activities, Gandhi’s arrival and the Rowlatt-Jallianwala hinge, Non-Cooperation, the Swarajists and No-Changers, the Civil Disobedience and the Salt March, the Round Tables and the Act of 1935, the provincial ministries, the Left (the CSP, the trade unions), the INA and Subhas Bose, the Quit India and the Cabinet Mission, and partition with independence — the contributors from every part of the country priced.
plannedLessons: Gandhi’s Arrival and the Mass Movements
The Left, the Revolutionaries and the INA
Modern Indian History: The Significant Events, Personalities and Issues

chapters.title: Post-Independence India
chapters.summary: The republic’s narrative decades (the analytical polity belongs to Political Science; the story lives here): partition’s aftermath and the princely states’ integration (Patel and Menon’s craft), the linguistic reorganisation, the official-language question, the Constitution’s framing and framing moments (cross-referenced), the planned economy and the Green Revolution, the wars with China and Pakistan and the nuclear turn, the non-aligned foreign policy (cross-referenced to International Relations), the Emergency, the coalition era and the LPG reforms — the GS1 ’post-independence consolidation and reorganisation’ line carried in full.
plannedLessons: The Planned Economy and the Green Revolution
The Wars and the Foreign-Policy Arc
The Emergency, Coalitions and the Reforms

chapters.title: The Culture Thread and the Doorstep
chapters.summary: The long thread that ran through every chapter — the art forms, literature and architecture from the Bhakti-Sufi worlds to the modern renaissance — gathered as one register and handed to Art History for the object-level depth and to Cultural Studies for the contemporary; the synthesis map of the whole chronicle; and the doorstep — to Political Science (the Constitution), to World History (the imperial arc this story was embedded in), and to the reader’s own family as the arc’s living continuation.
plannedLessons: The Doorstep: the Republic and Beyond

title: Political Science
subtitle: Power, ideas and the state — from political theory to the working of the Indian Constitution
description: The discipline in one arc. What politics is (power, authority, legitimacy, the state’s definitions) and the approaches; the political theory core — freedom, equality, social justice, rights, citizenship, secularism, nationalism as CONTESTED concepts each with their thinkers; the ideologies — liberalism, conservatism, socialism, nationalism, feminism, ecologism, with political economy and globalisation; democracy’s models and legitimacy, elections, representation, voting behaviour; constitutions, the rule of law, executives, legislatures, judiciaries and the separation of powers; then the Indian spine: the Constitution’s making, salient features, fundamental rights and duties, the federal structure, parliament, the executive and the judiciary, elections and the RPA, constitutional bodies; parties, pressure groups, political culture and identity politics; Indian political thought (Kautilya, Gandhi, Ambedkar, Aurobindo); the comparative glance; and the world-order pointer. Cross-references International Relations (the world-order depth), Public Administration (the governance machinery) and Law and Legal Studies (the constitutional-law depth) and hands off to the Humanities shelf’s Ethics for public-values register.

chapters.title: What Is Politics?
chapters.summary: The discipline’s first question answered four ways: politics as the exercise of power (the faces-of-power debate — the second and third faces priced), as the machinery of government, as the public sphere’s deliberation, as the allocation of values (Easton); authority’s types and legitimacy’s claim; the state’s definition and its sovereignty; and the approaches’ census — normative against empirical, behavioural, institutional, the political-economy lens — with the science’s method honestly cross-referenced to the Mathematics shelf’s statistics book.

chapters.title: The Concepts of Political Theory
chapters.summary: The theory core as contested concepts (the NCERT arc): freedom’s negative and positive readings (Berlin’s two concepts, Gandhi’s freedom as swaraj); equality’s kinds — formal, substantive, of opportunity against outcome; social justice from Rawls’s veil to Ambedkar’s annihilation; rights’ classifications and the rights-duties dialectic; citizenship from the polis to the diaspora; secularism’s western and Indian models; nationalism from Herder to the anti-colonial register — every concept taught as a live argument.

chapters.title: Ideologies and the Political Economy
chapters.summary: The ideologies’ register: liberalism’s classical and social-democratic wings; conservatism’s disposition; socialism from Marx through the social democrats to the actually-existing question; nationalism’s political work; feminism’s waves and the political; ecologism’s deep and shallow greens; the political economy — capitalism’s variants, the globalisation debate (the GS register’s effects-on-society lines cross-referenced to Sociology), the welfare state’s rise and crisis.

chapters.title: Democracy and Representation
chapters.summary: Democracy’s models — direct, representative, participatory, deliberative — with legitimacy’s performance crisis; the regime census (democratic, authoritarian, hybrid — the third-wave and its reversals); elections and representation’s theories (the trustee against the delegate, the mandate theory); voting behaviour’s sociological and economic models; parties and party systems (the Sartori census; India’s party system’s evolution from the Congress system to coalition to the present); and the pressure groups, movements and interests — Heywood’s register carried whole.
plannedLessons: Civil Liberties, Civil Rights and American Political Culture

chapters.title: Constitutions and Institutions
chapters.summary: The institutional core: constitutions as higher law (codified against uncodified — the Westminster against the US model), the rule of law and judicial review, judges’ role and the appointment debates; executives — presidential against parliamentary, the leadership question; legislatures’ structure, functioning, powers and privileges; the separation of powers and its checks; the comparison of the Indian constitutional scheme with other countries (the GS2 line) — the Westminster inheritance, the US bill of rights, the French laicite as three reference points.
plannedLessons: Constitutions and the Rule of Law
Foundations of American Democracy and the Branches of Government

chapters.title: The Indian Constitution
chapters.summary: The Indian text as politics: the historical underpinnings and evolution (the 1858-1947 acts compressed — the analytical register owned by Law and Legal Studies), the making (the Assembly’s craft), the salient features; the preamble’s keywords argued; the fundamental rights and duties with the DPSP’s balance; the basic-structure doctrine earned from Kesavananda; the amendments’ census; and the working of the rights in the courts — the Laxmikanth-Basu arc with the NCERT Constitution-at-Work pedagogy.
plannedLessons: The Making and the Salient Features
Rights, Duties and the Directive Principles

chapters.title: The Indian State at Work
chapters.summary: The machinery in action: the union and the states’ functions and responsibilities, the federal structure’s issues and challenges (the GS2 line — fiscal federalism’s devolution priced), the panchayati and municipal devolution; the parliament and state legislatures’ conduct of business; the executive and the judiciary’s structure and functioning; the Representation of People’s Act’s salient features; the constitutional posts and the statutory, regulatory and quasi-judicial bodies’ census.
plannedLessons: The Union Executive: President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
Parliament: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and Committees
Federalism, State Governments and Local Bodies
The Election Commission and Electoral Reforms
Constitutional and Statutory Bodies: CAG to UPSC

chapters.title: Identity Politics in India
chapters.summary: The political culture and the identity register: the political culture-media-identity triangle (Heywood’s chapter priced for India); the caste’s political career from Mandal to the present; the communalism and secularism’s political register (cross-referenced to Sociology’s society chapters); the regionalism and the sons-of-soil; the women’s political representation and the quota debate; and the political socialisation — how Indians become political animals.

chapters.title: Indian Political Thought
chapters.summary: The thought register the UPSC PSIR paper prices: Kautilya’s Arthashastra as statecraft (the mandala theory, the spy system, the danda); the Dharmashastras’ political ideas priced carefully; Gandhi’s swaraj, satyagraha and the oceanic circles; Ambedkar’s annihilation argument, the constitutional morality and the Buddha’s dhamma; Aurobindo’s integral freedom; Vivekananda, Tagore and Savarkar as the modern debate’s poles; and the Western canon’s Indian dialogues — the comparative thought register.

chapters.title: The World Order and the Doorstep
chapters.summary: The global register named and handed off: multilevel politics (the EU as the case), security’s domestic-international blur, world order and global governance — Heywood’s final chapters are the POINTER (the depth is International Relations’ whole book); the public policy and bureaucracy chapter as the POINTER to Public Administration; and the doorstep — to the comparative politics’ world (the AP US Government units as one reference), to International Relations for the inter-state order, and to the reader’s own political judgement.

title: International Relations
subtitle: Anarchy and its institutions — the theory and practice of the inter-state world
description: The inter-state world as its own discipline. The field’s birth (the Great War’s shock, the 1919 chairs) and its levels of analysis; the theories in full — realism classical and neo-, liberalism and the democratic peace, the English School, constructivism, Marxism and the critical theories, feminism, the post-positivist turn; war and security (the causes of war, the security dilemma, terrorism and WMD, collective security); the international history register (the modern order’s rise, the thirty-years crisis, the cold war — the NCERT Contemporary World Politics arc); international law and organisation (the UN system, the special agencies, the regional bodies, the NGOs); the global political economy (trade, finance, the WTO-IMF-World Bank trio, development’s regime); the environment and the human-security agenda; India and the world (the foreign policy’s evolution, the neighbourhood, the groupings, the diaspora — the GS2 lines 17-20 in full); the world order’s change; and the doorstep. Cross-references Political Science (the theory’s domestic twin) and World History (the order’s past) and hands off to the reader’s newsfeed.

chapters.title: The Discipline of IR
chapters.summary: The field’s own story: international relations born as a discipline from the First World War’s rubble (the 1919 Aberystwyth chair, the idealist-first age priced honestly); the core problem — anarchy (no world government, the self-help world) with the Westphalian myth interrogated (1648’s treaty read against its historiography); sovereignty’s meanings; and the levels of analysis (the individual, the state, the system — Waltz’s three images) as the book’s analytic spine.
plannedLessons: The Birth From the Great War

chapters.title: The Theories of IR
chapters.summary: The theoretical register in full: realism from Thucydides and Machiavelli through Morgenthau to neo-realism (Waltz’s structure) and the offensive-defensive debate; liberalism — the Kantian tripod, interdependence, the democratic peace; the English School’s international society; constructivism’s Wendtian turn (anarchy is what states make of it); the radical family — Marxism, dependency, world-systems; feminism and gender in IR; the post-positivist and critical turn — every theory taught with its counter.
plannedLessons: The Radical Family and the Critical Turn

chapters.title: War and Security
chapters.summary: Security’s register: war’s causes priced (the levels applied — Thucydides’ fear-honour-interest to the bargaining model); the security dilemma and the offence-defence balance; deterrence’s logic and its nuclear age (the stability-instability paradox named); terrorism and the WMD proliferation; collective security’s idea and its record (the League’s failure priced); and the changing security concept — the Buzan widening from state to human (the NCERT security chapter’s arc).

chapters.title: The International History Register
chapters.summary: The order’s past told as IR (the narrative depth owned by World History, the interstate logic here): the modern international order’s rise from the European concert; the thirty-years crisis 1919-1949 (Versailles, the League, the appeasement); the cold war’s structure (the containment, the crises, the détente and the ending — the NCERT cold-war chapters as the spine); the post-cold-war unipolar moment; and the present multipolar question — each era read through the theories of chapter two.
plannedLessons: The Concert to the Thirty-Years Crisis

chapters.title: International Law and Organisation
chapters.summary: The legal-institutional register: international law’s sources and its enforcement problem (the anarchy’s law); the treaties’ life and the states’ consent; the UN system in full — the Charter’s structure, the Security Council’s arithmetic and the veto, the Assembly, the Secretary-General’s political role, the peacekeeping’s record, the reform debate; the special agencies’ census (the WHO, the ILO, the UNICEF family); the regional organisations (the EU’s sui generis, the ASEAN, the African Union); and the NGOs and the global civil society — the GS2 ’international institutions, agencies and fora — their structure and mandate’ line carried in full.
plannedLessons: The NGOs and the Global Civil Society

chapters.title: The Global Political Economy
chapters.summary: IPE’s register: trade’s regimes from the GATT to the WTO (the dispute settlement priced); finance’s order — the Bretton Woods system, its collapse, the IMF and the World Bank’s roles and their critiques; the global production’s chains and the South’s development question (the dependency register revisited); the sanctions’ weapon; and the economic statecraft’s present (the weaponised interdependence named) — the economic THEORY is cross-referenced to the Economics shelf’s future books, this book owns the political reading.
plannedLessons: Trade: From GATT to the WTO
The Sanctions and the Weaponised Interdependence

chapters.title: The Environment and Human Security
chapters.summary: The agenda’s widening: the climate regime’s history (the IPCC, the UNFCCC, the Paris architecture and its loss-and-damage debate); the environmental negotiations’ North-South structure; the migration and refugee regime (the 1951 convention’s limits); the health security register (the pandemic as the security event); the human security doctrine’s rise and its critique; and the resources — water, energy, the rare earths as the geopolitical stakes.

chapters.title: India and the World
chapters.summary: The applied register (GS2 lines 17-20 in full): India’s foreign policy evolution — the Nehruvian non-alignment and Panchsheel, the 1962-1971 wars’ lessons, the nuclear turn, the post-cold-war reorientation, the present multi-alignment; India and its neighbourhood — the Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Myanmar, Afghanistan relations priced as a set; the diaspora’s policy (the GS2 line); and the groupings — from the BRICS and SCO to the Quad and the I2U2 with the multilateral ledger (the NSG bid, the G20 host’s arc).
plannedLessons: The Groupings and the Multilateral Ledger

chapters.title: The World Order and the Doorstep
chapters.summary: The changing order’s synthesis: the rise of China as the system’s biggest question (the Thucydides trap’s framing priced honestly); the Russia-West rupture and the Ukraine war’s order effects; the global South’s claim; the technology and the order (the chips, the AI — the CS shelf’s books cross-referenced for the tech); globalisation’s political future; and the doorstep — to Political Science for the domestic twin, to World History for the past, to the reader’s own newsfeed as the living text this whole book was written to help read.
plannedLessons: The Rise of China and the Order
The Ruptures and the Global South

title: Public Administration
subtitle: The machinery of government — from Kautilya and Wilson to the e-office and the citizen’s charter
description: The governance machinery as its own discipline. The field’s meaning, scope and significance (the art-science debate, the public-private divide, the development-administration concept); the administrative thought’s full register — Kautilya’s Arthashastra, Woodrow Wilson’s essay, Weber’s bureaucracy, Taylor and Fayol’s management, the Hawthorne turn, Simon’s decisionism, the later thinkers; administrative behaviour (motivation, leadership, communication, morale, the decision craft); the organisation theories’ census; accountability and control (the legislative, judicial and executive tools, the ombudsman, the RTI); the Indian administration’s spine (the constitutional framework, the PMO and ministries, the civil services, the state-district administration, the local government after the 73rd/74th amendments); planning, the budget’s craft and financial administration; the policy cycle and implementation science; e-governance and the service delivery’s reform; and the public personnel and ethics handshake. Cross-references Political Science (the constitutional organs’ political reading) and hands off to Ethics (the probity register) and to the reader’s own city office.

chapters.title: The Discipline of Public Administration
chapters.summary: The field’s own questions: administration’s meaning and scope (the POSDCORB census as the classic answer); the art-or-science debate priced; the public-private divide (the publicness criterion — what makes an organisation public); the development administration concept (the Riggsian ecology and the prismatic society named); Wilson’s 1887 essay as the field’s founding shot (the politics-administration dichotomy he proposed and later thinkers dismantled); and Nicholas Henry’s five paradigms as the field’s self-understanding — where the discipline has been and what it lost on the way.
plannedLessons: The Meaning and the POSDCORB Census

chapters.title: The Administrative Thought
chapters.summary: The thinkers’ full register: Kautilya’s Arthashastra as the first administrative text (the saptanga theory, the machinery of the spy state — priced as administration not just statecraft); Weber’s bureaucracy as the ideal type (the hierarchy, the files, the merit, the iron cage critique); Taylor’s scientific management and Fayol’s fourteen (the classical school); the Hawthorne studies and the human relations turn (Mayo, Maslow’s hierarchy, McGregor’s X-Y, Herzberg’s two factors); Simon’s bounded rationality and the decision school; and the later — Dror’s planning, Riggs’ ecology, the New Public Administration’s equity turn.
plannedLessons: The Classical School and the Human Relations Turn

chapters.title: Administrative Behaviour
chapters.summary: The office’s psychology and flow: motivation’s theories applied to the public service (the pecuniary and the purposive); leadership’s styles in the administrative setting (the transformational against the transactional); the communication’s web (the formal and the grapevine, the barriers, the e-office’s effect); morale and its measurement; the decision-making craft — the rational model’s limits, the incremental (muddling through), the mixed scanning; and the group dynamics in committees (the groupthink trap priced).

chapters.title: The Organisation Theories
chapters.summary: The organisation’s census: the classical (Weber, Taylor, Fayol as the machine); the neoclassical (the human relations as the correction); the systems theory (the organisation as an open adaptive system — the inputs-throughputs-outputs model); the contingency theory (no one best way — the structure follows the task); the post-modern and the critical turn (the Osborne-Gaebler reinvention named); and the public organisation’s own peculiarities — the multiple conflicting objectives, the measurement problem, the sovereignty’s shadow.

chapters.title: Accountability and Control
chapters.summary: The leash’s register: the legislative control (the question hour, the committees — the estimates and the public accounts, the CAG’s audit as the legislature’s eye); the judicial review’s administrative reach (cross-referenced to Law and Legal Studies); the executive’s internal control (the vigilance, the hierarchy); the ombudsman’s idea and the Indian variants (the Lokpal and the Lokayuktas priced); the citizens’ participation and the transparency revolution — the RTI’s architecture and its use; and the e-governance accountability (the digital trail) — the GS2 ’important aspects of governance, transparency and accountability’ line carried in full.
plannedLessons: The Legislative Control and the CAG
The Ombudsman’s Idea and the Lokpal
The RTI and the Transparency Revolution

chapters.title: The Indian Administration
chapters.summary: The Indian machine’s own anatomy: the constitutional framework’s administration (the All-India Services’ constitutional home); the PMO and the Cabinet Secretariat as the apex; the ministries and departments’ anatomy (the secretariat pattern, the attached and subordinate offices); the civil services’ craft (the steel frame’s history, the recruitment, the training, the conduct rules and the AIS acts); the state administration; the district collector’s office as the field’s apex; and the local government after the 73rd-74th amendments (the three-tier panchayat, the municipal finance’s problem — the devolution’s actual record priced honestly).
plannedLessons: The Apex: PMO and Cabinet Secretariat
The Collector and the Local Government

chapters.title: Planning and Financial Administration
chapters.summary: The money’s machinery: the planning’s evolution (the Commission era, the NITI’s cooperative federalism turn); the budget’s craft — the stages (formulation, enactment, execution), the types (line-item against performance and zero-based), the Indian budget’s anatomy, the deficit vocabulary; the financial administration’s control system (the CAG’s audit types, the public accounts committee’s follow-through); the public debt and the FRBM’s discipline; and the government accounting’s cash-and-accrual debate priced at survey depth.
plannedLessons: The CAG and the PAC’s Follow-Through
The Debt and the Fiscal Discipline

chapters.title: Policy and Implementation
chapters.summary: The policy’s life: the cycle (the agenda setting, the formulation, the legitimation, the implementation, the evaluation — the model’s limits priced); the implementation science (the street-level bureaucrat’s discretion, the principal-agent chains, the last-mile problem with Indian case studies — the MGNREGA’s and the DBT’s registers); the policy analysis’ tools (the cost-benefit, the stakeholder mapping); the e-governance’s models (the G2C, G2B, G2G census with the successes, the limitations and the potential — the GS2 line); the citizens’ charters and the service delivery’s quality (the Sevottam’s arc); and the reforms — the New Public Management and the good-governance agenda.
plannedLessons: The Policy Cycle and Its Limits
Government Policies, Interventions and the Development Industry
Welfare Schemes for Vulnerable Sections: Poverty and Hunger

chapters.title: The Personnel, the Ethics Handshake and the Doorstep
chapters.summary: The people’s register and the close: the personnel administration (the recruitment’s merit methods, the training’s arc, the performance appraisal’s problem, the promotion and the seniority-merit debate, the conduct and the disciplinary machinery); the ethics handshake — the integrity’s institutionalisation (the vigilance’s architecture, the CVC and the Lokpal named) with the VALUES register handed to Ethics (the GS4 book) and the administrative accountability staying here; the future — the administrative culture’s change, the AI in government (the CS shelf’s books cross-referenced); and the doorstep — to the reader’s own city office, the eye that now knows what the file on the counter actually is.
plannedLessons: The Doorstep: The Reader’s Own Office

title: Law and Legal Studies
subtitle: The rule book and its reasoning — jurisprudence to the working law of the Indian republic
description: Law as a discipline and a craft. The legal map first (law’s definitions, the sources, the families — common law against civil law, the customary and the religious, the Indian system’s mixed parentage); the jurisprudence register (the natural law, positivist, historical, sociological and realist schools with the Hart-Fuller debate and the critical theories); the constitutional law depth (the Constitution’s structure, the rights and remedies, the amendment’s engine — the political reading cross-referenced to Political Science, the legal reading owned here); the administrative law (the delegated legislation, the natural justice, the judicial review); the private-law census (contract, tort and the commercial law’s core); the criminal law (mens rea and actus reus, the IPC’s general principles, the procedure’s frame); the international law register; the legal reasoning craft (the IRAC method, the case reading, the statutory interpretation, the fact-situation logic for the CLAT register); the profession’s own world (the courts’ hierarchy, the advocate’s ethics, the ADR); and the contemporary developments. Cross-references Political Science and hands off to the reader’s own rights as the living text.

chapters.title: The Legal Map
chapters.summary: Law’s own introduction: what law is (the definitions from Austin’s command to the sociological register), the sources’ census (legislation, precedent, custom — the binding and the persuasive); the legal families (the common law’s case method against the civil law’s code, the religious and the customary systems); the Indian legal system’s mixed parentage (the Anglo-Saxon frame over the customary strata priced honestly); the courts’ hierarchy and the jurisdiction’s map; and the legal profession’s own sociology — who makes law and for whom.
plannedLessons: The Courts’ Hierarchy and the Profession

chapters.title: Jurisprudence
chapters.summary: The theory of law’s schools: the natural law’s long arc (Aquinas to Finnis’s modern restatement); the positivist age — Austin’s command theory, Kelsen’s pure norm, Hart’s primary and secondary rules with the open texture; the historical school (Savigny’s Volksgeist); the sociological (Ehrlich’s living law, Pound’s engineering); the realists (the American and the Scandinavian); the Hart-Fuller debate and Hart-Devlin’s — law’s morality questioned; and the critical family — CLS, the feminist jurisprudence, the post-colonial legal critique (the Indian registers named).
plannedLessons: The Critical Family and the Hart-Fuller Debate

chapters.title: Constitutional Law
chapters.summary: The Constitution’s legal reading: the constitution as higher law and the amendment’s engine; the fundamental rights’ text and the courts’ growth of them (the due-process arrival, the expansion from Maneka onward — the leading cases priced as craft); the remedies (the habeas corpus family — Article 32 as the fundamental of fundamentals); the directive principles’ justiciability debate; the federal structure’s legal form (the seventh schedule’s division, the articles 3 question, the fiscal federalism’s legal frame); and the emergency provisions’ legal history — the ADM Jabalpur lesson and the 44th amendment’s answer.
plannedLessons: The Rights and the Courts’ Growth

chapters.title: Administrative Law

chapters.title: Unity and Diversity

plannedLessons: The Monera, Protista and Fungi: Salient Features and Classification
Lichens, Viruses and Viroids: The Edge of the Five Kingdoms

chapters.title: The Ecological Frame
chapters.summary: The biosphere’s architecture introduced: the individual in its environment (biotic and abiotic factors); the population and its growth logic; the community as the interacting cast; the ecosystem as the flow of energy and the cycling of matter; and the biosphere as one system — with the honest warning that ecology-and-full register belongs to the ecology book and plant-ecology owns the botanical lines, this chapter sets the frame every later book hangs from.

chapters.title: The Biologist’s Craft
chapters.summary: The working skills: the field notebook and the observation’s discipline; the dissection and microscopy lab register with the safety craft; the data table, the graph and the statistical mean as the honest tools of a school-level biologist; the specimen’s collection and the herbarium’s idea (the plant-taxonomy book owns the full register); and the career map — the researcher, the doctor, the ecologist, the biotechnologist and the teacher as the shelf’s downstream doors.

chapters.title: The Doorstep
chapters.summary: The ground floor’s close: the shelf’s map drawn one final time — the core books (cell, molecular, genetics, evolution, ecology, biotechnology, microbiology, immunology) each previewed in a paragraph; the botany and zoology shelves named as the two great organism traditions; the NEET register’s weight honestly stated (biology as the exam’s heaviest half) with the NCERT lines named as the school spine; and the promise that the next book — cell biology — opens the machinery that everything else in biology hangs from.
plannedLessons: The Promise of the Next Book
Adolescence, Drug and Alcohol Abuse: The Health Register

title: Cell Biology
subtitle: The fundamental unit of life, fully told — structure, membranes, communication and division
description: The cell as biology’s atom: the theory and the tools that established it (light and electron microscopy, cell fractionation); the prokaryotic architecture against the eukaryotic; the plasma membrane’s fluid-mosaic structure and its transport census — diffusion, osmosis, facilitated diffusion and the active pumps; the endomembrane system (nuclear envelope, ER, Golgi, lysosomes) as the eukaryote’s manufacturing and shipping network; mitochondria and chloroplasts as the energy organelles with their own DNA and the endosymbiotic explanation; the cytoskeleton’s three fibres and the extracellular matrix; the cell cycle with mitosis as division of the nucleus, meiosis as division for sex; and cell signalling — how cells receive, transduce and respond to messages.

chapters.title: The Theory and the Tools
chapters.summary: The cell doctrine and its evidence: Hooke’s cork, Leeuwenhoek’s animalcules, Schleiden and Schwann’s generalisation and Virchow’s omnis cellula e cellula; why the theory needed the microscope — resolution against magnification as the two separate limits; the light microscope’s craft and its staining register; the electron microscope’s two kinds (transmission for ultrastructure, scanning for surfaces); and cell fractionation — how the centrifuge assigns each organelle its own layer and each layer its own job.
plannedLessons: Cellular Energetics: Enzymes, Energy and Respiration

chapters.title: The Prokaryotic Architecture
chapters.summary: The small cell’s honest completeness: the nucleoid as the gene region without a membrane; the ribosomes as the protein factories in their 70S size; the cell wall-and-peptidoglycan craft with the Gram stain as the physician’s oldest quick test; the capsule, the fimbriae and the flagellum as the attachment-and-motion register; the plasmid as the small extra circle that carries resistance — the clinical and biotechnological consequences deferred to their owning books; and the endospore as survival’s hardest form.
plannedLessons: The Wall and the Gram Craft

chapters.title: Membranes and Transport
chapters.summary: The boundary’s craft: the fluid-mosaic model — phospholipid bilayer as the sea, proteins as the icebergs with their two orientations, cholesterol as the temperature’s moderator; the selective permeability logic; passive transport’s census (simple diffusion, osmosis with its tonicity arithmetic — hypotonic, isotonic, hypertonic in plant and animal cells; facilitated diffusion through channels and carriers); active transport’s engine (the sodium-potassium pump as the nerve’s battery charger, electrochemical gradients); and bulk transport — endocytosis and exocytosis as the cell’s swallowing and shipping.

chapters.title: The Endomembrane System
chapters.summary: The manufacturing network: the nuclear envelope with its pores as the information gate; the endoplasmic reticulum’s two faces (rough with ribosomes as the protein factory, smooth as the lipid-and-detox line); the Golgi apparatus as the postal sorting centre with its cis and trans faces; lysosomes as the recycling stomach with the Tay-Sachs register priced honestly; vacuoles — the plant cell’s water tower; and vesicular traffic as the whole system’s bloodstream, with the secretion path traced from ribosome to plasma membrane.
plannedLessons: The Two Faces of the ER

chapters.title: The Energy Organelles
chapters.summary: The power plants and their origin: mitochondria as the respiration site (double membrane, cristae, matrix, its own circular DNA); chloroplasts as the photosynthesis site (thylakoids, grana, stroma) with the plastid family beyond; the endosymbiosis theory’s evidence — double membranes, own DNA, own ribosomes, binary fission, and the divide-and-conquer logic of an ancient engulfment; and the inheritance honesty: mitochondrial DNA passed mother-to-child, the register the genetics book prices at its chapter on extranuclear inheritance.

chapters.title: The Cytoskeleton and the Matrix
chapters.summary: The cell’s bones and its yard: the three fibre systems — microtubules (the mitotic spindle’s rails and the flagellum’s core), microfilaments (actin’s muscle-and-motion engine) and intermediate filaments (the tensile rope); motor proteins as the fibre-walkers (kinesin and dynein, myosin’s walk); the extracellular matrix as the collar — collagen, the integrin connections and the tissue’s informational yard; cell junctions (tight, desmosomes, gap) as the tissue’s three ways of holding and talking; and the walls of plant cells and the bacterial peptidoglycan cross-referenced to their owning books.
plannedLessons: Cilia, Flagella, Centrioles and the Nucleus Register

chapters.title: The Cell Cycle and Mitosis
chapters.summary: Growth by copying: the cycle’s phases (G1, S, G2, M) with the checkpoints as the quality gates and cyclin-CDK as the clock’s molecular engine; DNA replication deferred to molecular-biology (this chapter needs only its fact); mitosis as the equal division — prophase’s chromosome condensation (chromatids, centromeres, the kinetochore), prometaphase’s capture, metaphase’s one-cell-equator alignment, anaphase’s sister separation, telophase’s two nuclei; cytokinesis’s two crafts (the animal cleavage furrow against the plant cell plate); and the significance: two genetically identical cells.

chapters.title: Meiosis — the Division for Sex
chapters.summary: The reduction division: why sex demands a halving (fertilisation restores — the alternation of generations logic); meiosis I as the homologue’s separation — synapsis, the tetrad, crossing over as the swap that makes every chromosome a mosaic, independent assortment as the second shuffle with its 2-to-the n arithmetic; meiosis II as the sister’s separation; the outcomes — four genetically distinct gametes; the errors (non-disjunction) priced honestly with Down syndrome as the register the genetics book inherits; and the comparison table against mitosis set straight once.

chapters.title: Cell Communication
chapters.summary: The signal register: the three stages — reception, transduction, response — as the universal architecture; the receptors (G-protein-coupled as the largest family, receptor tyrosine kinases, ion-channel and intracellular for the hormones that pass membranes); transduction as the phosphorylation cascade (the relay runner metaphor priced honestly — one activated enzyme amplifying to thousands); the second messengers (cAMP, calcium) as the cascade’s fuel; and response — from enzyme activation to gene expression, with apoptosis as the programmed exit that development needs.

title: Molecular Biology
subtitle: The central dogma fully told — DNA, RNA and the protein-making machinery of every living thing
description: The information system at full depth: DNA as the double helix — the Watson-Crick structure with its base-pairing arithmetic, the semi-conservative replication the Meselson-Stahl experiment proved, the replication factory (helicase, polymerase, the leading and lagging strand-and-Okazaki craft, the proofreading that keeps fidelity near-perfect); transcription from gene to RNA (the promoter, RNA polymerase, the three RNA products); translation as the genetic code’s reading (the codon table’s 64 entries, the tRNA adapter, the ribosome’s three sites, initiation through termination); the regulation register — operons in prokaryotes, transcription factors and enhancers in eukaryotes, the chromatin’s open-and-closed states; mutation and repair as the error economy; and the mobile elements with retrotransposons as the genome’s restless fraction; the applied tools (restriction enzymes, PCR, CRISPR) are cross-referenced to biotechnology, and the heredity patterns above the molecule belong to genetics.

chapters.title: The DNA Structure
chapters.summary: The double helix earned: the nucleotide’s anatomy (deoxyribose, phosphate, the four nitrogenous bases — purines against pyrimidines); Chargaff’s two rules as the arithmetic clue; the Watson-Crick model as the deduction that fit everything — antiparallel strands, the sugar-phosphate backbone outside, the A-T and G-C pairs inside with their hydrogen-bond counts; the semiconservative prediction and the Meselson-Stahl density-gradient proof; and the packing craft — from naked duplex to nucleosomes (the histone octamer) to the chromosome’s coiled heights, with the bacterial circle contrasted.

chapters.title: The Replication Factory
chapters.summary: The copying machine: the origin as the starting bubble; helicase as the unzipper and single-strand-binding as the stabiliser; DNA polymerase’s chemistry (the 5-to-3 direction only, the need for a primer); the leading strand’s continuous run against the lagging strand’s Okazaki fragments with ligase as the final welder; the telomere honesty — eukaryotic ends that shorten each division, telomerase as the germ-and-cancer exception; the proofreading and mismatch-repair register with the error rate’s astonishing arithmetic; and the enzymes-as-census table fixed once and drilled.

chapters.title: Transcription — from Gene to RNA
chapters.summary: The first reading: RNA polymerase’s binding at the promoter (the TATA register) with the transcription factors’ assembly in eukaryotes; the elongation craft (the template strand read 3-to-5, the new RNA built 5-to-3); termination’s signals; the three products — mRNA as the courier, tRNA as the adapter, rRNA as the ribosome’s own scaffold-and-catalyst; and the eukaryotic processing register (the 5 cap, the poly-A tail, the intron splicing with the spliceosome) — the prokaryote-eukaryote contrast that makes the comparison table worth fixing.

chapters.title: Translation — the Code Read
chapters.summary: The protein factory: the genetic code’s properties (triplet, read in frames, degenerate — the wobble honesty, universal with its near-universality exceptions honestly stated); the codon table fixed by drill (the AUG start, the three stops, the table’s use and abuse in exam questions); the tRNA’s craft (the anticodon, the aminoacyl-tRNA-synthetase charging — the enzyme that actually knows the code); the ribosome’s three sites (A, P, E) with initiation-elongation-termination walked once slowly; and the post-translational register — folding, modification, targeting to organelles.

chapters.title: The Prokaryotic Regulation
chapters.summary: The operon’s economy: Jacob and Monod’s lac operon as the classic — the promoter, the operator, the repressor’s shape change on lactose, the positive cAMP-CAP register when glucose is scarce; the trp operon as the repressible mirror; the regulatory logic’s two families (inducible against repressible) with the exams’ both-ways questions priced; the finer control — attenuation and riboswitches named; and the significance: the bacterium’s budget — making only what the environment demands.

chapters.title: The Eukaryotic Regulation
chapters.summary: The orchestrated genome: chromatin’s states (acetylation opening, methylation’s two meanings, the histone code named at survey depth); the transcription factors’ census (the general assembly at the promoter, the specific ones binding enhancers up to a million bases away with the DNA-looping craft); the RNA-level register (alternative splicing as one gene-many proteins, miRNA’s silencing, mRNA breakdown control); protein-level control named; and the differential-expression honesty — why a liver cell and a neuron carry the same genome yet differ entirely.

chapters.title: Mutation and Repair
chapters.summary: The error economy: the mutation census (point — silent, missense, nonsense; frameshift by insertion-deletion; the chromosomal scale deferred to genetics); the causes (base analogs, radiation’s thymine dimers, the chemical mutagens) with the Ames test as the carcinogen screen; the repair census (proofreading, mismatch, excision repair with the xeroderma-pigmentosum honesty, the SOS response in bacteria); the mutation’s double face — mostly neutral, occasionally terrible, rarely the raw material of evolution; and the rate’s arithmetic priced honestly.
plannedLessons: The Causes and the Ames Screen

chapters.title: Mobile Elements and Viruses
chapters.summary: The genome’s restless fraction: transposons — the cut-and-paste DNA kind and the copy-and-paste retrotransposons (LINEs and SINEs as nearly half the human genome-and-honest census); the viral life’s chemistry-only edge (the capsid, the envelope, the genome’s DNA-or-RNA and double-or-single register); the bacteriophage’s lytic against lysogenic cycles; retroviruses with HIV as the reverse transcriptase’s carrier (the clinical register deferred to the medical shelf); and the horizontal-gene-transfer idea — conjugation, transformation, transduction — as the bacterial world’s promiscuity, the biotechnology book’s opening door.

chapters.title: Genomes and the Doorstep
chapters.summary: The book’s close at survey depth: the genome sizes’ census (from viruses through bacteria to the eukaryotic C-value surprise); the human genome’s map at headline depth (the ~20,000 genes against the 98-percent non-coding honesty and what that fraction is now known to do); the model genomes named (E. coli, yeast, Arabidopsis, the fly, the worm, the mouse); genomics’ methods deferred to biotechnology (sequencing, the databases, the comparison register); and the doorstep — to genetics for the patterns above the molecule, to biotechnology for the tools, to the medical shelf for the clinical registers.
plannedLessons: The Human Map at Headline Depth

title: Genetics
subtitle: Heredity from Mendel to the genome — transmission, extension, population and the quantitative register
description: The heredity discipline in one arc: Mendel’s logic — the garden-pea experiments with their meticulous ratio arithmetic (segregation 3:1, independent assortment 9:3:3:1), the test-cross detective craft and the probability laws that carry every prediction; the extensions’ census — dominance hierarchies, incomplete dominance and codominance, multiple alleles (the ABO craft), pleiotropy and epistasis, polygenic inheritance and the environment’s fingerprint; the chromosome theory — Morgan’s fly room, linkage and the recombination arithmetic that builds genetic maps, sex linkage and the Barr body; extranuclear inheritance (the mitochondrial and chloroplast registers); the pedigree and the probability counselling craft; population genetics (the Hardy-Weinberg engine, the five forces that move allele frequencies); and the quantitative and epigenetic registers named honestly.

chapters.title: Mendel’s Logic
chapters.summary: The monastery’s arithmetic: the pea’s seven traits and the true-breeding start; the monohybrid cross — P to F1 to F2 with the 3:1 ratio and its hidden 1:2:1 genotypic spine; the dihybrid 9:3:3:1 as the independent-assortment receipt; the vocabulary fixed (gene, allele, homozygous, heterozygous, genotype, phenotype) because every later chapter leans on it; the test cross as the detective’s tool (the unknown genotype exposed by the recessive cross); the probability craft (the product and sum rules, the Punnett arithmetic from one square to two); and why Mendel counted — quantification as biology’s then-new move.
plannedLessons: The Seven Traits and True Breeding

chapters.title: The Extensions’ Census
chapters.summary: Mendel’s clean ratios, complicated honestly: dominance hierarchies (complete, incomplete with the snapdragon’s pink, codominance with the ABO blood craft and its transfusion arithmetic); multiple alleles as the population-level truth (three alleles, six genotypes, four phenotypes of the ABO system); pleiotropy (the sickle allele’s many effects — the clinical honesty deferred); epistasis (the 9:3:4 and 12:3:1 modifications); polygenic inheritance with the bell curve (skin colour and height as the continuous register); and the environment’s fingerprint (the hydrangea’s soil-pH colour, the Siamese cat’s temperature-darkened points) — the norm-of-reaction idea.
plannedLessons: Polygenic Curves and the Norm of Reaction

chapters.title: The Chromosome Theory
chapters.summary: The fly room’s evidence: Sutton’s parallel (the alleles’ behaviour mirrors the chromosomes’ behaviour); Morgan’s white-eyed fly as the first sex-linked proof (the X-chromosome logic); the linkage honesty — the genes that ride the same chromosome and the crossing over that sometimes separates them; the recombination frequency as the map distance (the 1-percent-equals-one-map-unit arithmetic) with a two-point and three-point cross walked; the map’s construction as the cumulative receipt; sex determination’s census (the XY and WZ systems, the haplodiploid bees, the temperature reptiles); and the Barr body with the dosage-compensation idea.

chapters.title: The Chromosome Errors
chapters.summary: The karyotype’s craft and its failures: the chromosome census fixed (the human 46, the banding craft); non-disjunction’s consequences — Down (trisomy 21), Klinefelter (XXY), Turner (XO) with their phenotype honesty; the structural errors (deletion, duplication, inversion, translocation with the Robertsonian craft and the familial-Down translocation carrier); the polyploid register (fatal in animals, the plant breeder’s friend — cross-referenced to plant-genetics); and the ethics register priced once — the counselling, the screening, the decisions, with the medical-shelf cross-reference named.
plannedLessons: The Polyploid Split and the Ethics
The Mendelian and Chromosomal Disorders: Thalassemia to Klinefelter

chapters.title: The Extranuclear Inheritance
chapters.summary: Beyond the nucleus: the cytoplasmic maternal lines — chloroplast variegation (the four-o’clock-leaf’s branches) and the mitochondrial pedigrees (the maternal-only transmission, the heteroplasmy honesty, the LHON register as the clinical example); the infectious heredity of the kappa particle in Paramecium named at survey depth; and the modern receipt — the endosymbiotic explanation (why the organelle keeps its own tiny circle) with the mitochondrial-DNA applications (the Eve register, the forensic identity craft cross-referenced to forensic-medicine).

chapters.title: The Pedigree and the Counselling Craft
chapters.summary: The family tree as instrument: the pedigree’s symbols and the autosomal-dominant, autosomal-recessive and X-linked patterns read from the tree itself (the vertical against the horizontal transmission, the male-only and the criss-cross registers); the probability counselling craft (the carrier arithmetic, the Bayesian updating at survey depth); consanguinity’s honesty; the Mendelian errors of the pedigree (the reduced penetrance and variable expressivity named); and the diagnosis register deferred to the medical shelf (the amniocentesis, the CVS, the newborn screening named without duplication).
plannedLessons: The Symbols and the Three Patterns

chapters.title: The Population Register
chapters.summary: The allele’s fate in the crowd: the Hardy-Weinberg engine (the p²-2pq-q² equilibrium, the five conditions of its stillness) with the allele-frequency arithmetic drilled on real numbers; the five forces — mutation’s trickle, migration’s gene flow, drift’s sampling error (the bottleneck and founder registers with their real-world examples), selection’s directional-stabilising-disruptive census, and non-random mating; the fitness arithmetic; and the honesty — why the equilibrium is a null model: the biologist’s way of asking, what is moving this population?

chapters.title: The Quantitative and the Epigenetic
chapters.summary: The continuous traits and the marks above the sequence: quantitative genetics’ craft — the normal distribution, heritability’s two meanings (broad and narrow) with the selection-response arithmetic (R = h²S) priced at survey depth, the twin studies’ logic and their honesty (the equal-environment caveat); epigenetics’ register — DNA methylation and histone marks as the switches above the code, the genomic imprinting (the Igf2 case), the agouti mouse’s dietary demonstration, the transgenerational honesty still contested; and the modern synthesis’ frame — genes and environment meeting in the statistic.
plannedLessons: The Twin Studies’ Logic and Limits

chapters.title: The Genomic Doorway
chapters.summary: The transmission register’s close: the association craft (GWAS at headline depth — the SNP chips, the hits and their small effects honesty); the pharmacogenomic idea named; the gene drive’s logic and its ethics (the mosquito registers); the genome editing deferred to biotechnology (the CRISPR craft owned there); and the shelf’s map drawn — molecular-biology beneath (the machinery), plant-genetics beside (the breeding exploitation), the medical shelf above (the clinical registers), the evolution book ahead (the population forces at species scale). The genetics register holds: heredity is arithmetic plus evidence, and both have been earned.

title: Evolution
subtitle: Descent with modification — the evidence, the mechanisms, the speciation and the history of life
description: The unifying theory as a working discipline: the evidence register — fossils and their dating, the homology census (anatomical, molecular, developmental with the Hox depth), biogeography’s island logic, direct observation in the resistance era; the mechanism at population depth (variation’s sources, selection’s three modes, drift and its registers, the fitness arithmetic honestly defined); speciation’s craft — the barrier concept (prezygotic and postzygotic census), allopatric against sympatric with the polyploid plant register, the rate and pattern debate (gradualism against punctuated equilibrium priced fairly); phylogenetics and systematics — the tree-building craft (shared derived characters, the clade’s logic, the molecular clock at survey depth); macroevolution’s trends; the origin of life-and-chemical register at survey depth; human evolution honestly told; and coevolution’s webs.

chapters.title: The Evidence Register
chapters.summary: The case built from four independent lines: the fossil record with its absolute (radiometric) and relative dating, its gaps honestly stated and its transitional forms (the whale’s land-to-sea arc, the feathered dinosaurs); homology — the same bones in the human arm, the bat wing and the whale flipper, the molecular homologies (the same genes across the tree, the cytochrome-c ladder), the developmental homologies (the pharyngeal arches and the Hox names); biogeography — the island registers (Darwin’s Galapagos, Wallace’s line), the continental-drift receipt; and direct observation — the resistance era as evolution watched in real time.
plannedLessons: The Fossil Arc and Its Dating

chapters.title: Variation and Selection
chapters.summary: The mechanism’s engine room: variation’s sources (mutation’s trickle, the sexual recombination’s shuffle — why sex is evolution’s accelerator); selection’s three modes (directional, stabilising, disruptive with their curve arithmetic); fitness honestly defined as reproductive success, not strength; the selection’s receipts — industrial melanism’s peppered moth, the sickle-cell’s malaria balance, the antibiotic resistance story priced as evolution’s fastest case; sexual selection (the peacock’s tail, the intrasexual combat, the runaway honesty); and the microevolution arithmetic connecting to the population engine of the genetics book.
plannedLessons: Darwin's Contribution and the Modern Synthetic Theory

chapters.title: Drift, Flow and the Neutral Register
chapters.summary: The non-selective forces: drift as sampling error (the small-population honesty — the bottleneck’s northern elephant seal, the founder’s Amish polydactyly register, the fixation of alleles by coin-flip not merit); gene flow’s homogenising current (the migration arithmetic); the neutral theory of molecular evolution (Kimura’s claim — most fixation at the molecular level is drift, the nearly-neutral refinement) priced as the theory it is; and the relative-rates honesty — which force dominates at which population size, with the conservation consequences named.

chapters.title: The Origin of Species
chapters.summary: The multiplication of lineages: the species concept census (biological, morphological, phylogenetic, ecological — each honest about its failures); the barrier census — prezygotic (temporal, habitat, behavioural, mechanical, gametic) against postzygotic (the reduced-viability-fertility registers); allopatric speciation as the mainstream (the geographic barrier, the divergence, the secondary contact’s outcomes — fusion, reinforcement, the stable hybrid zone); sympatric speciation-and-honest registers (the polyploid plants as the instant species, the cichlid lakes, the host-shift insects); and the rate debate (gradualism against punctuated equilibrium, both kept as pattern claims).

chapters.title: The Tree-Building Craft
chapters.summary: Systematics as the discipline that reads ancestry: the character honesty (shared ancestral against shared derived — the homoplasy trap: convergence, reversal); the clade’s logic (monophyletic only, the paraphyletic and polyphyletic traps named); the tree-reading craft (nodes, sister taxa, the rooting); the methods at survey depth (maximum parsimony, maximum likelihood, the Bayesian register named); the molecular clock (its assumptions, its calibration, its error bars honestly stated); and the three-domain tree as the current consensus map, with the LGT honesty that complicates the deep tree.
plannedLessons: The Clock and Its Error Bars

chapters.title: The Grand Pattern
chapters.summary: Above the species line: the trends’ honesty (complexity’s passive drift claim, the Cope’s-size and the Dollo’s-irreversibility claims each priced as the debated propositions they are); extinction’s register — the background rate and the five (arguably six) mass extinctions with their causes (the end-Permian, the K-Pg asteroid) and their recoveries; adaptive radiation’s engine (the post-extinction emptiness, the island arrivals — the cichlids and the honeycreepers as receipts); the Cambrian explosion’s honesty (the fossil reality, the older-soft-body explanation, the eye-and-predation hypotheses); and the macroevolution-microevolution linkage kept honest.

chapters.title: The Origin of Life
chapters.summary: The chemical register at survey depth (the chemistry shelf owns the depth): the Miller-Urey experiment and what it did and did not show; the RNA world’s logic (the molecule that is both information and machine — the ribosome’s RNA core as the receipt); the protocell idea (the fatty-acid vesicles, the first heredity); the metabolic-first against replicator-first debate priced as the live one it is; and the history-of-life timeline fixed (the ~3.5-billion-year microbes, the oxygen revolution, the eukaryotic engulfment, the multicellular explosions) — each register told honestly as what the evidence supports.

chapters.title: The Human Story
chapters.summary: The lineage told straight from the fossils: the hominin frame (bipedalism first — the Australopithecus receipt, the brain later); the genus Homo’s census (the erectus’ global reach, the habilis’ tools, the Neanderthal’s own story — the DNA receipt of interbreeding, the Denisovans); the Out-of-Africa replacement against multiregional debate settled to the mostly-replacement-with-gene-flow honesty; the culture engine (the tool kits’ three ages, fire, language, the symbolic explosion); and the race honesty — the genetic variation within against between populations, the one-species register that undercuts the old race science.
plannedLessons: The Culture Engine and the Race Honesty

chapters.title: Coevolution and the Webs
chapters.summary: The entangled registers: the coevolution census (mutualism’s reciprocal crafts, the arms races of predator-prey and parasite-host, the mimicry registers — Batesian and Mullerian with their arithmetic); the plant-pollinator web (the orchid-and-deceptive craft, the pollinator’s reward economics — the plant books’ cross-reference); the Red Queen’s logic (the never-ending race that explains sex); the geographic mosaic idea (the patchy coevolution) named at survey depth; and the evolutionary ecology bridge — the ecological book’s communities read as the coevolution’s arena.

title: Ecology
subtitle: The biosphere’s architecture — organisms, populations, communities, ecosystems and their conservation
description: The environmental discipline in full: the organism in its habitat (the abiotic filters — temperature, water, light, the tolerance curves); biomes as the climate’s great formations; population ecology — the growth models (exponential and logistic with their carrying-capacity arithmetic), the life-history strategies (r and K), the metapopulation idea, the human population’s demographic transition honestly told; community ecology — the interaction census (competition with the niche and Gause’s principle, predation and its defences, the mutualisms), the succession register, the diversity patterns (island biogeography’s arithmetic, the latitudinal gradient); ecosystem ecology — energy’s one-way flow through trophic levels with the 10-percent honesty, matter’s cycles (carbon, nitrogen, the phosphorus sediment trap), the climate-change register; and conservation — the biodiversity crisis, the protected-area craft, the restoration registers.

chapters.title: The Organism and Its Environment
chapters.summary: The individual’s filters: the abiotic register (temperature, water and its availability, light, soil and its chemistry, the fire and wind factors) with each factor’s tolerance curve and its upper-lower limits; the adaptation census (physiological — the kangaroo rat’s water economy, morphological, behavioural); the acclimatisation against adaptation honesty; the biome census at map depth (the tropical forest, savanna, desert with its plant-and-animal receipts, temperate forest, taiga, tundra, the two great water realms — with the aquatic zones from littoral to abyssal); and the climate engine (the latitudinal solar arithmetic, the rain-shadow craft) as the biome maker.

chapters.title: The Population’s Arithmetic
chapters.summary: The counting discipline: the census craft (the quadrat and mark-recapture with their arithmetic, the transect); the distribution patterns (clumped — the reality, random and uniform priced); the growth models — exponential (the J-curve’s premise) against logistic (the S-curve with its carrying capacity and the density-dependent honesty); the density-independent shocks (the weather and fire registers); the life-history census (r-strategy against K-strategy with the honest continuum caveat, the survivorship curves’ three shapes); the metapopulation idea (the source-and-sink patchiness); and the human population told straight — the demographic transition, the age-structure pyramids, the carrying-capacity debate.
plannedLessons: The Census Craft and Its Arithmetic
Population Attributes: Growth, Birth and Death Rates

chapters.title: The Interaction Census
chapters.summary: The community’s relationships: competition — the niche concept (the fundamental against the realised), Gause’s principle earned by the Paramecium experiments, the character displacement receipt (Darwin’s finches’ beaks); predation and its defences (the cryptic and warning colour, the mimicry cross-reference, the hunting strategies); herbivory’s plant-defence register (the chemical and the thorn-and-spine, cross-referenced to the plant books); the mutualism census (the pollination, the mycorrhiza, the coral-zooxanthella, the gut flora); and the parasitism register deferred to the parasitology book’s own depth; each interaction priced by its ecological arithmetic, not as storytelling.

chapters.title: Communities and Succession
chapters.summary: The cast and its changes: the community’s measurable properties (species richness, the diversity indices’ craft — Simpson and Shannon at survey depth); the succession register — primary (the bare rock’s lichen beginning) against secondary (the field-to-forest return), the seres’ stages with their tolerance-facilitation-inhibition explanations honestly weighed; the trophic-structure preview (the food chains and webs as the community’s economics — the full energy arithmetic owned two chapters ahead); the island-biogeography theory (the species-area and the equilibrium of arrivals against extinctions, the reserve-design consequence); and the latitudinal diversity gradient named as ecology’s oldest unsolved pattern.
plannedLessons: The Two Successions and Their Stages
